assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a genuinely new observational window: a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice that detects high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This is the kind of instrument-driven discovery I value most, built on years of calibration and background control, and it is astroparticle physics at its core. The diffuse flux, the blazar association and the Galactic-plane result give the field a clear scientific legacy.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept and Karle was central to the construction and the analysis of the discovery. The supplied credit supports a two-person prize; the large collaboration and other early leaders (AMANDA/IceCube founders) mean the allocation would need care and I cannot independently verify the full history.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse astrophysical flux was reported around 2013 and has been confirmed by other analyses and channels; the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 associations and Galactic-plane emission extend it. Independent confirmation from other detectors (e.g. in water) is still growing but the discovery itself is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Source identification is still partial, so the 'neutrino astronomy' interpretation is not fully mature.
Whether a two-name credit fairly represents the decisive contributors is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic peak is a standard ruler that turned galaxy surveys into precision cosmology and underpins dark-energy measurements. It is a clear, original measurement result with lasting impact on how the expansion history is probed.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections by the SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Peacock) teams were simultaneous and independent, which supports a fair trio. Theoretical prediction credit (early work by others) may be argued but is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly by SDSS/BOSS/eBOSS, 6dF, WiggleZ and recent DESI; very mature, and recognition is not premature. The recent DESI hints about evolving dark energy do not undermine the BAO measurement itself.
uncertainties: Survey-collaboration credit is diffuse and may complicate selection of at most three people.
Prior theoretical work on acoustic features is outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties at the 1e-18 level and enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. A high-precision measurement technology of exactly the sort I respect.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance to record levels with strontium; this is a compact, defensible two-person credit. Other groups (e.g. ion-clock and neutral-atom competitors) contribute to the wider field but are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent clocks worldwide agree at the 1e-18 level and are used in comparisons, so the result is well confirmed. Redefinition of the second is pending, so applications are still maturing, though the physics is stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition in optical frequency combs and ion traps may affect committee appetite.
Credit relative to other lattice-clock groups is not assessed from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered full-sky microwave-background maps and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level. A big step in precision cosmology, built on careful systematics control, although the field already recognised COBE and the later Planck data refined the numbers.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel the cosmological analysis and Page the instrument and early design; this maps well onto mission leadership, theory and instrumentation. Other WMAP team members and the Planck leaders make the allocation less clean.
assessment.maturity: Results were confirmed and improved by Planck and ground experiments, so it is very mature. The risk is that its novelty relative to COBE and the 2019 cosmology prize area may reduce the case.
uncertainties: Whether WMAP is seen as a discovery or a refinement of an earlier recognised result.
Credit among a large collaboration and versus Planck leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* required a planet-sized VLBI array at 1.3 mm and demanding calibration and imaging methods. It is an impressive instrument achievement with a clear public impact and consistent with general relativity.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT effort and Moran contributed the foundational VLBI/mm-wave work. The collaboration spans hundreds of people, so a three-name credit is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and results have been reproduced by independent imaging pipelines, but the physical interpretation (spin, jets, ring structure) is still evolving and the observations are only a few years old; arguably early.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit and imaging-method contributions are hard to apportion.
Interpretation of the images is model dependent and still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers (SASE concept to LCLS, European XFEL) produce femtosecond coherent X-ray pulses and opened time-resolved structure and ultrafast science. A major accelerator-based instrument with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini and Kim are tied to SASE and high-gain FEL theory and Rossbach to the TESLA/FLASH development; the supplied trio is plausible but the 1980s theory (Bonifacio et al.) and the LCLS builders could be argued.
assessment.maturity: Facilities operate worldwide with many results, so maturity is high. The enabling-technology character means it is judged on the instrument as much as discovery.
uncertainties: Disputed priority between theory and machine builders.
Fit as a physics discovery versus a facility technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links foundational quantum ideas to secure communication and now to satellites and networks. I give it weight because I value concrete uses of fundamental physics, but this is outside my expertise and I would rely on colleagues for the foundations.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol are the conceptual core; Jian-Wei Pan is the leading experimental implementer. A three-person prize would leave out either the experimental or a conceptual credit.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated over long distances and by satellite, with commercial systems; practical security against real-device attacks remains a topic of study.
uncertainties: Real-world security and the status of the networks are unresolved.
Outside my own expertise, so my assessment is weak.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing arrays have detected evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic sources, and a precision-timing achievement I find attractive as an experimentalist.
assessment.attribution: Credit sits across NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA; McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester represent the three regional efforts but the key analysis authors are many.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is only around 3-4 sigma and the origin of the signal is not settled; waiting for higher significance and the Hellings-Downs curve confirmation seems prudent. Probably premature now.
uncertainties: Detection significance and astrophysical origin are unsettled.
